blocks.text: Supabase stores table data in PostgreSQL and exposes APIs around it. A browser client asks those APIs for allowed data.

Use the Supabase local CLI with its required container runtime, then run supabase init and supabase start in a practice project. Use the local URL and public key reported by its status command. SQL runs in the local database tools.

blocks.code:
Browser page -> Supabase API -> PostgreSQL table
The public client key identifies the project.
Row-level security decides which rows the client role may access.
blocks.title: Know the database and the client

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: The browser talks to a project API rather than holding a database-owner connection.
The database checks the role and row policy before returning allowed records.

blocks.text: The worked flow separates the browser request from the database permission check.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: A public project key is not a substitute for row-level security. Never place a service-role or secret key in browser code.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Point to where row permissions are checked in the flow.
